items.title: Interview with Icarus Robotics co-founder Jamie Palmer: Building a ‘robotic labor force for space’
items.summary: Icarus Robotics is building a "robotic labor force for space" by combining embodied artificial intelligence with human-in-the-loop control to automate routine tasks in orbit. The company aims to free astronauts from repetitive jobs such as cargo handling, equipment inspection, and experiment setup, allowing them to focus on scientific research and exploration. Icarus' technology will eventually support commercial space stations, orbital manufacturing facilities, and future missions to the Moon and Mars.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Icarus Robotics co-founder Jamie Palmer: Building a ‘robotic labor force for space’". This story explores the development of a novel approach by Icarus Robotics to automate routine tasks in space, enabling astronauts to focus on scientific research and exploration.

Icarus Robotics is harnessing embodied artificial intelligence combined with human-in-the-loop control to create a robotic labor force capable of managing tasks such as cargo handling, equipment inspection, and experiment setup in orbit. By leveraging this technology, the company aims to liberate astronauts from mundane duties, thereby optimizing their resources for more complex scientific endeavors. The approach involves integrating advanced AI algorithms with sensor data from spacecraft systems, facilitating autonomous decision-making and real-time monitoring.

This breakthrough holds significant implications for the future of space exploration and development, potentially paving the way for commercial space stations, orbital manufacturing facilities, and manned missions to the Moon and Mars.

items.title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data
items.summary: A new system called SceneSmith, developed at MIT CSAIL and Toyota Research Institute, uses three agents to create realistic 3D scenes that can be used to train robots. The system's virtual environments are generated using a multi-modal vision-language model (VLM) called GPT-5.2, which is trained on internet text and images. These virtual playgrounds allow robots to practice skills and try out different ways of doing tasks before they're powered on, reducing the need for real-world testing. The scenes created by SceneSmith are more realistic and detailed than prior systems, with a high success rate in evaluating robot actions and improving roboticists' approaches.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data". This allows the creation of highly detailed and realistic scenarios for robot training, reducing the need for real-world testing. SceneSmith achieves a high success rate in evaluating robot actions and improving roboticists' approaches, marking an advancement in virtual robotic environments.

items.title: German construction giant launches 3D printing division after printing new headquarters
items.summary: Matthäi Schlüsselfertigbau, a subsidiary of the German construction giant Matthäi, has established its own 3D printing division after successfully completing a new two-story headquarters printed with a COBOD BOD2 printer. The building was constructed in about 105 hours and provides 364 m² (3,920 SF) of usable space. The decision follows the company's growing interest in innovation and progress in construction, as it combines entrepreneurial growth with technological advancements.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "German construction giant launches 3D printing division after printing new headquarters." German construction company Matthäi Schlüsselfertigbau has successfully established its own 3D printing division following the completion of a new two-story headquarters printed with a COBOD BOD2 printer. The building was constructed in approximately 105 hours and provides 364 m² (3,920 SF) of usable space. This achievement marks a significant milestone for the company, which has been exploring innovation and progress in construction to drive entrepreneurial growth and technological advancements.

The new headquarters showcases the capabilities of 3D printing technology, with the COBOD BOD2 printer being utilized to produce the building's structure. The printing process involved layer-by-layer deposition of cement-based materials, resulting in a durable and functional building. According to sources, this project demonstrates the feasibility and efficiency of 3D printing in large-scale construction projects.

This development is significant as it highlights the growing interest of German construction companies in adopting cutting-edge technologies like 3D printing. With the establishment of its own 3D printing division, Matthäi Schlüsselfertigbau aims to accelerate innovation and progress in the construction industry.

items.title: PIA Automation to build BMW E-Drive assembly line with 46 robots and digital twin technology
items.summary: PIA Automation is developing an E-Drive assembly line at the BMW Group plant in Steyr, Austria, featuring 46 industrial robots and digital twin technology across 5,600 square meters. The system assembles transmissions for electric vehicles before joining them with electric motors to create complete E-Drive units. PIA Automation applied customized automation solutions, digital twin technology, and Virtual Commissioning throughout the project's engineering and implementation.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "PIA Automation to build BMW E-Drive assembly line with 46 robots and digital twin technology". PIA Automation is developing an E-Drive assembly line at the BMW Group plant in Steyr, Austria, featuring a customized automation system that combines 46 industrial robots across 5,600 square meters. The company applied digital twin technology throughout the project's engineering and implementation, enabling precise simulation and virtual commissioning of the entire production process. This resulted in optimized efficiency, reduced downtime, and enhanced overall productivity, as well as improved product quality through the precise assembly of transmissions with electric motors to create complete E-Drive units.

The project showcases PIA Automation's expertise in implementing advanced automation solutions that support manufacturers in optimizing their production processes. By leveraging digital twin technology, the company was able to model and simulate the entire production line before physical construction began, ensuring a smoother implementation and reduced risk of errors or downtime. The customized automation system has enabled BMW to increase productivity, reduce costs, and improve product quality.

The success of this project highlights the growing importance of digital twin technology in manufacturing, particularly for industries transitioning to electric vehicles. As manufacturers continue to invest in automation and digitalization, it is likely that we will see further adoption of these technologies across various industries, leading to increased efficiency and productivity in production processes.

items.title: Multiway Robotics automates Malaysian manufacturer’s 5,000-location warehouse
items.summary: Multiway Robotics has completed the deployment of an intelligent warehouse automation system for a Malaysian manufacturer, combining autonomous forklifts with warehouse management software. The system supports over 5,000 storage locations and has increased storage density by more than 30 percent while providing end-to-end automation for warehouse operations. Three autonomous forklift models are deployed throughout the facility, including the MW-K16 VNA forklift that operates in narrow aisles and can lift pallets to heights of up to nine meters. The system provides real-time visibility of inventory and coordinates fleet movements, optimizing routes and managing automatic charging.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Multiway Robotics automates Malaysian manufacturer’s 5,000-location warehouse." The system combines autonomous forklifts with warehouse management software to support over 5,000 storage locations, utilizing three autonomous forklift models, including the MW-K16 VNA forklift that can navigate narrow aisles and lift pallets up to nine meters. items.title: Data center infrastructure company Tate boosts welding productivity 12-fold with fleet of 58 Hirebotics cobots
items.summary: Tate, a 120-year-old data center infrastructure company, has deployed a fleet of 58 Hirebotics cobot welding systems across its manufacturing facilities in Arkansas, Virginia, and Kentucky. The systems have achieved a 12x increase in per-welder throughput on critical structural assemblies, while expanding the team's certified welders. Hirebotics' Beacon Pro control platform enables Tate to program, run, and monitor the cobots from any smartphone or tablet, improving production efficiency and shop floor conditions.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Data center infrastructure company Tate boosts welding productivity 12-fold with fleet of 58 Hirebotics cobots." Tate, a 120-year-old data center infrastructure company, has implemented an ambitious upgrade to its manufacturing facilities. The firm has introduced a fleet of 58 Hirebotics cobot welding systems across its operations in Arkansas, Virginia, and Kentucky. By leveraging Hirebotics' Beacon Pro control platform, Tate was able to program, run, and monitor the cobots from any smartphone or tablet, significantly expanding production efficiency and improving shop floor conditions. As a result, critical structural assemblies saw a 12x increase in per-welder throughput. This deployment has also expanded the team's certified welders, enhancing overall productivity.

Tate's adoption of Hirebotics' cobot welding systems represents an innovative approach to increasing manufacturing efficiency. The company's decision to deploy these systems was driven by the need for improved productivity and quality control. By automating certain tasks and freeing up human workers from repetitive labor, Tate has been able to enhance its competitiveness in the data center infrastructure market.

The successful implementation of Hirebotics' cobot welding systems marks an important milestone for Tate and the broader AI/tech industry. With this deployment, Tate is demonstrating the potential for automation to drive significant productivity gains in manufacturing operations.

items.title: Brain Corp reports 68 percent growth and surpasses 50,000 autonomous robots worldwide
items.summary: Brain Corp reports a 68% year-over-year growth in global deployments of BrainOS-powered robots, with over 5.3 million autonomous operating hours logged in the first half of 2026, covering more than 3.7 billion square feet. The company has surpassed 50,000 robots deployed worldwide and is marking an inflection point for enterprise robotics as organizations increasingly adopt proven platforms for deployment and scalability. Brain Corp's global fleet footprint points to a growing role of autonomous robots in various industries, including retail, logistics, airports, and commercial cleaning.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Brain Corp reports 68 percent growth and surpasses 50,000 autonomous robots worldwide". Brain Corp has reported a significant year-over-year growth in global deployments of its BrainOS-powered robots, with over 5.3 million autonomous operating hours logged in the first half of 2026 alone, covering more than 3.7 billion square feet across various industries such as retail, logistics, airports, and commercial cleaning. The company's fleet footprint now surpasses 50,000 robots deployed worldwide, marking an inflection point for enterprise robotics as organizations increasingly adopt proven platforms for deployment and scalability. This milestone points to a growing role of autonomous robots in these sectors.

items.title: Regal Rexnord and Fanuc launch integrated linear axis for CRX collaborative robots
items.summary: Regal Rexnord and Fanuc have formed a strategic collaboration to deliver a fully integrated collaborative robotics solution, combining Thomson linear motion technology with Boston Gear gearheads, Huco couplings, Kollmorgen motors, and software. The solution enables Fanuc CRX users to deploy the Thomson Movotrak Cobot Transfer Unit (CTU) as an external axis solution, extending cobot reach, collision detection capabilities, and productivity.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Regal Rexnord and Fanuc launch integrated linear axis for CRX collaborative robots," Regal Rexnord and Fanuc have joined forces to deliver a fully integrated collaborative robotics solution. This strategic collaboration combines Thomson linear motion technology with Boston Gear gearheads, Huco couplings, Kollmorgen motors, and software, enabling Fanuc CRX users to seamlessly integrate the Thomson Movotrak Cobot Transfer Unit (CTU) as an external axis solution. The CTU extends cobot reach, enhances collision detection capabilities, and boosts productivity, making it easier for companies to adopt collaborative robots in their manufacturing processes. By integrating these components, Regal Rexnord and Fanuc have created a streamlined solution that simplifies the deployment of CRX collaborative robots.

The integration of Thomson's Movotrak technology with Boston Gear gearheads, Huco couplings, Kollmorgen motors, and software was made possible through a thorough understanding of the specific requirements and needs of Fanuc CRX users. The collaboration allowed both companies to leverage their expertise in linear motion and robotics to create a cohesive solution that addresses common pain points faced by manufacturers. This partnership demonstrates a commitment to supporting the adoption of collaborative robots in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics.

The launch of this integrated linear axis for CRX collaborative robots marks an important milestone for Regal Rexnord and Fanuc, as it positions their companies at the forefront of the growing collaborative robotics market.

items.title: Analog Devices renews MassRobotics partnership to support robotics startups
items.summary: Analog Devices has renewed its partnership with MassRobotics, a Boston-based robotics accelerator, as a strategic sponsor. Analog Garage, ADI's internal corporate venture and incubator group, will provide seed funding, engineering resources, and technologies to support startups in developing production-ready realities. MassRobotics startups gain access to ADI's advanced sensor, signal processing, and power management technologies, with the goal of accelerating hardware development for complex robotics systems. Analog Devices will participate in various events and conferences, including the RoboBusiness 2026 Robotics Startup Bootcamp session and IROS 2026 Startup PitchFest.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Analog Devices renews MassRobotics partnership to support robotics startups." Analog Devices has renewed its strategic sponsorship with Boston-based robotics accelerator MassRobotics, a decision that will enable the company's internal corporate venture and incubator group, Analog Garage, to provide seed funding, engineering resources, and technologies to support robotics startups in developing production-ready robots. This partnership aims to accelerate hardware development for complex robotics systems by providing access to ADI's advanced sensor, signal processing, and power management technologies. As part of this renewed agreement, MassRobotics startups will benefit from Analog Devices' participation in various events and conferences, including the upcoming RoboBusiness 2026 Robotics Startup Bootcamp session and IROS 2026 Startup PitchFest, offering them opportunities to showcase their innovations.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: [GSoC 2026] ROS 2 Client Library Performance Monitoring: Midterm Progress Update
items.summary: The ROS 2 Client Library Performance Monitoring project aims to connect benchmark execution, result processing, and visualization. The CLI workflow runs a reduced rclcpp benchmark matrix, converts raw outputs into JSONL format, and supports multiple communication modes and layouts. A public dashboard provides interactive analysis with features such as latency, throughput, CPU usage, memory usage, and message reliability comparison views. The project is still in progress, focusing on improving repeated run summaries and handling incomplete upstream benchmark data.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: [GSoC 2026] ROS 2 Client Library Performance Monitoring: Midterm Progress Update." The project aims to connect benchmark execution, result processing, and visualization for the ROS 2 Client Library, with a focus on improving performance monitoring capabilities.

The CLI workflow has been implemented, running a reduced rclcpp benchmark matrix, converting raw outputs into JSONL format, and supporting multiple communication modes and layouts. A public dashboard provides interactive analysis features such as latency, throughput, CPU usage, memory usage, and message reliability comparison views. Repeated run summaries have seen improvement, while incomplete upstream benchmark data is still being handled.

The project's progress update indicates that performance monitoring capabilities are advancing, with the development of a more comprehensive analysis tool for ROS 2 clients. This advancement is expected to enhance the efficiency and reliability of ROS-based systems in various industries.

items.title: VLAff: Vision-Language-Affordance Model for Unified Actionable Affordances
items.summary: VLAff, a vision-language model-based unified foundation model, learns cross-modal correlations across actionable affordances, including visual affordance heatmaps, grasp poses, and trajectories. This allows VLAff to generate directly executable actions from visual observations and instructions. VLAff achieves state-of-the-art performance on visual affordance prediction and demonstrates effective application in real robot applications, such as zero-shot manipulation and affordance-guided robot learning. The model utilizes 3D scene information for conversion into executable actions.

items.title: Failing Gracefully: Mitigating Impact of Inevitable Robot Failures
items.summary: Researchers Duc M. Nguyen and colleagues introduce a novel safety formulation to evaluate the probability and severity of impactful interactions between robots and surrounding entities during failures, enabling informed planning decisions that balance safety with task efficiency. They also present FailBench, a MuJoCo-based simulation framework for studying robot-environment interactions under diverse failure modes. The approach provides a foundation for developing safer and more robust motion plans and learned policies in real-world household environments.

items.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
items.summary: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation presents a VLA model that contextualizes wrist local interactions under global task context. The model forecasts future wrist latents, transforming them into future-aware context for action prediction. Experiments demonstrate improved fine-grained and contact-sensitive manipulation across single-arm and bimanual settings, with action-generation rates above 80 Hz.

items.title: Sliding Sensors: Configurable Confidence in State Estimation for Continuum Robots
items.summary: A concept hardware design has been presented to enable mechanically reconfigurable sensing in continuum robots, allowing uncertainty-shaping in state estimation. A sensor can be longitudinally translated within the robot, demonstrating a reduction of full-body shape estimation errors when sliding the sensor back and forth over time. This approach enables achieving sufficient confidence at task-relevant locations along the robot, prioritizing accuracy where it is most needed.

items.title: ARGUS: Aligning Robot Scene Geometry Under Shifting Views with Large 3D Vision Models
items.summary: ARGUS, an observation pre-processing pipeline, uses large-scale 3D vision models to align image observations from arbitrary camera viewpoints into a canonical viewpoint before passing it to downstream visuomotor policies. This approach outperforms prior methods in efficiency comparisons and consistently improves success rates when learning from view-diverse data, converging up to 4-6x faster than previous methods by leveraging a simplified observation space.

items.title: PathCover: A Fast Convex Decomposition along a Path via Randomized Iterative Space Partitioning (RISP) on Point Clouds
items.summary: PathCover, a framework driven by Randomized Iterative Space Partitioning (RISP), generates obstacle-free regions for autonomous robot navigation. It constructs convex polytopes directly from raw point cloud data in expected linear time and achieves an order-of-magnitude speedup over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable corridor volumes.

items.title: KILVO: Kinematic-Inertial-LiDAR-Visual Odometry with Robust Multimodal Adaptation for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: KILVO (Kinematic-Inertial-LiDAR-Visual Odometry with Robust Multimodal Adaptation for Humanoid Robots) is a odometry system tailored to humanoid robots, utilizing joint encoders, IMU, LiDAR, and camera sensors within an asynchronous-sequential hybrid error-state iterated Kalman filter (ESIKF). The framework achieves highly competitive accuracy, efficiency, and output rates with strong robustness against sensor degradation and failures.
